item.title: An Alaska storm scattered artifacts. Archaeologists are racing to save what's left
item.description: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
item.description: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

item.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
item.description: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

item.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
item.description: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

item.title: US and Denmark reach deal to build US military presence in Greenland
item.description: President Donald Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

item.title: Editor Rose Friedman, who helped shape NPR's cultural coverage, dies at 38
item.description: Friedman was in her early 20s when she landed her first position as an editorial assistant at NPR. She became an editor and reporter, and a co-creator of the annual Books We Love reading guide.

item.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
item.description: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

item.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
item.description: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

item.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
item.description: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.
